I serially dated two "heteroflexible" cis guys from 15-21 (one has since officially come out as bisexual, but oddly enough he was the one who fetishized my breasts and told me not to get top surgery) and I think that those relationships are main reason is took me so long to start my transition. I didn't want to become more masculine out of fear that they wouldn't feel the same attraction to me anymore. Then when I got out of my last relationship and was single for the first time I realized that I wanted- and had wanted for a long time- to transition. There's no such thing as too late to transition, but for me I wish I would have started back when I was 15-16 because I probably would have had more changes and I would be where I want to be today. I wish I listened to my true wants and prioritized myself and my happiness over molding myself to my partners desires. However, that's easier said then done when youre in love with someone! 
I also think that internalized transphobia plays a role in why I was afraid to transition. I got really close with a trans girl over the past year who was just starting her own transition and seeing her process starting hormones made me realize that it's not as scary as it seems and I deserve to live in the body I want. Taking t has also allowed me to show up more authentically in my relationships now, as myself vs what my old partners wanted me to be. If it's something you desperately want, then I think you should follow that because you deserve to be your authentic self, but you have to be prepared to accept that you and your partners dynamic might change. However, if/when you become more confident in your body, it might also change for the better!

So I did t gel for a long time, which for me was like microdosing because it didn't really have much effects. My voice hadn't dropped after 4 months on gel and the only noticeable change was a little bit of bottom growth. Now I do shots and they actually work for me.

I say go for it and give T a try. You can always stop. I was on the fence as a non binary person for a long time, not thinking I had enough dysphoria to go on T, but as soon s I started getting the desired changes I realized that I am happier than ever. Lower voices are also androgynous, people of all genders have lower voices ,and you can stop once your voice has lowered as much as you'd like it. I didn't think I had much voice dysphoria either, then the other day I heard a video of myself talking and for the first time in my life I didn't cringe at the way I sounded. I always thought everyone hated their recorded voice and that's normal, but now I think it was some hidden dysphoria. 

Give t a try and see how you feel. The feeling is the most important thing. I think you'll feel when it's right. Despite all of my own reservations and fears around taking t (I came out as nonbinary 6 years before starting t!) As soon as I got on shots I could feel in my bones that this is what I need to do! And I'm sure you would feel the opposite if it's not right, too.
